title: [QST] cuDF Query is too slow
body:
Hi All,

I recently ported a script to use cuDF dataframes in place of pandas dataframes. On comparing the time taken by API calls, I found panda APIs to be doing much better. Honestly, I am confused by seeing such results. I am not sure if I have done it correctly, as this is my first time using cuDF. For your reference:

1. temp = cudf_df.query('Id == @i')
The Id column is int64 type, dataframe contains around 12 rows.
This query took:  **0:00:01.262744**


2. temp=pandas_df[pandas_df['Id']==i]  
The Id column is int64 type, dataframe contains data identical to cudf dataframe.
This query took:  **0:00:00.006388**

**System Configuration**
cuDF package version: cudf-cuda100  0.6.1 
NVIDIA CUDA toolkit version:  CUDA Version 10.0.130 with CUDA Patch Version 10.0.130.1
GPU Name: Titan RTX
Operating System: Linux
Architecture: x86_64
Distribution: Ubuntu
Version: 18.04.3 

cudf query API is almost 200 times slower. Could someone please point me in the right direction? 
Thanks in advance!
author: GoyalMansi

comments.body: thanks for your question! You probably need thousands of rows minimum to see a speedup. For small data frames, the overhead of launching a kernel on the GPU will be larger than the overhead of calling a function on the CPU. 12 rows is miniscule.
Thank you, that does make a lot of sense. Maybe, I need to find a better use case for cuDF then. Thanks Mark for the reply!

@GoyalMansi additionally it looks like you installed an old version of cuDF via pip as opposed to the latest version from conda. Would highly recommend installing from conda if/when you try cuDF again!

satisfaction_conditions: An explanation for why cuDF is significantly slower than pandas for small datasets
Guidance on appropriate use cases for cuDF vs pandas
Information about minimum dataset sizes needed to see GPU performance benefits

_classification.category: Requires build environment but hard to be dockerized
